correctness.rationale: Exact factorization S=XY with YX=H provides the complete cubic. Explicit characteristic coefficients were independently reconstructed and exhaustively checked for all 1016 words of lengths 3 through 9 using exact integer arithmetic. E/sqrt(n) tends to standard normal independently of limiting endpoint signs; adjacent switch densities A/n and B/n tend to 1/4 by a one-dependent law of large numbers. Polynomial-root continuity proves the scaled spectral limit, and solving the three conditional quadratics proves the exact 1/sqrt(2) atom with mass erf(1)/4. The source supplies uniform bounds n-1<=rho(M)<=n. Limits require analytic arguments, not simulations.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2026 paper already defines the canonical M and orientation-weighted S and gives individual signed trace examples; these are credited inputs. The newly proved random-word limit for rho(S)/sqrt(n), including a probability atom erf(1)/4, is not stated in its inspected sections. The closest published full results bound unsigned Parry spectrum and classify physical switch laws, respectively; neither implies random signed spectral distribution. Rugh–Tan weights and zeta identities do not specify this random-word three-branch mixture. Historical equivalents remain a material documented priority risk.
residual_risks: Related general signed kneading or random low-rank matrix literature could contain an equivalent unpublished or unindexed specialization; broad searchable sources do not prove its absence.
For the general weighted zeta literature the inspected main theory and definitions were sufficient to identify different stated results, but not every appendix or all historical citations were read.
The symbolic signed zeta is not automatically the geometric periodic-point zeta without boundary corrections.

value.rationale: Orientation-weighted signed periodic path counts in a high-entropy canonical Markov family are a natural measure of cancellation absent from unsigned entropy. The result identifies a sharp square-root rather than linear spectral scale and an explicit positive-probability atom caused by a complex-root transition. These are structural, parameter-free asymptotic predictions and cannot be read from existing unsigned cubic entropy counts without the new random-sign analysis.
